subject: ventures/parcel-dim-weight-calculator
professional: a parcel shipping / rate analyst at a 3PL or e-commerce fulfilment team who audits UPS, FedEx and USPS invoices. First checks: is the cube built from sides rounded to the nearest inch before multiplying, is billable weight the ceiling of max(actual, dim), does the divisor match the carrier and service (139 account / 166 retail and USPS, USPS only above 1 cu ft), and are the Additional Handling / Large Package / maximum bands the carriers' own (48 in, 30 in, 105 in L+G; 130 in L+G or 96 in length; 108 in / 165 in).

evidence.correctness: Ran the engine (node /tmp/claude-0/round94-parcel/tool.mjs) on 9 cartons and recomputed each in an independent Python script (/tmp/claude-0/round94-parcel/indep.py) written from the published carrier rules (UPS Rate and Service Guide / FedEx Service Guide: each side to nearest whole inch, cube/139, billable = ceil of the greater; Additional Handling >48 in longest, >30 in second, >105 in length+girth; Large Package/Oversize >130 in length+girth OR >96 in length; maximum 108 in / 165 in). Cube and billable weight agreed on all 9 at both 139 and 166 (16x12x10 @4 lb: 1,920 in3, 14 lb; 12.5^3: 2,197, 16 lb; 12.4^3: 1,728, 13 lb; 10^3 @3.01: 8 lb). Bands agreed on 8 of 9: 97x8x8 (length+girth 129) is a Large Package by the 96 in length rule, the tool said additional-handling (defect 0). The large-package flag text also claimed the 90 lb minimum is 'usually well above' the billable weight even at 195 lb (30x30x30). At a 166 divisor the tool applies dim weight to a 12x12x12 / 2 lb parcel (11 lb) where USPS bills 2 lb (no DIM at or under 1,728 in3), with no warning. Main number right, banding wrong in one rule: 2.
evidence.completeness: Every README feature runs end to end: billable weight per package and total (per-package round-up multiplied, checked 3 x 14 = 42), pounds of air, break-even cube (556 in3) and height (2.90 in) with the 'smaller box, not flatter' case, girth and three surcharge bands, dimension rounding toggle, share link round trip, local opt-out usage. No TODOs or stubs. The surcharge banding is complete except the 96 in length trigger.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 52/52 pass before the fix (59/59 after). Seeded 5 mutants with quality_mutate.py in calc.mjs: Math.round -> Math.ceil in side rounding SURVIVED (the only rounding test, 12.6, rounds to 13 either way); large-package '>' -> '>=' SURVIVED; second-side AH check on the shortest side SURVIVED; airWeight without Math.ceil(actual) SURVIVED; billable ceil -> round caught. 4 of 5 core mutants survived: 1. All four are killed by tests added this session.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (185 lines), levers.mjs, share.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script, all test files. Small, pure engine imported by the page (not reimplemented), strict positive/whole-number validation, finite-value guard, storage wrapped in try/catch, levers escaped as fixed templates. Defects: the value called 'girth' is length plus girth (carrier girth is 2W+2H), the heightAtDimWeight null branch is unreachable for positive inputs although its comment says it fires when the footprint prices above the goods (levers.mjs's 1.5 in threshold does that job).
evidence.claims: Backed: 14 lb / 10 lb of air / 556 in3 / 2.9 in worked example (content-pages.test.mjs ties copy to engine); no network requests (index.html has no fetch/XHR); disclaimer on page, explainer and README ('planning estimate, not a quote', no-warranty footer); served copy clean (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin). Not backed: README, FAQ and explainer described 166 only as a negotiated divisor when it is the published USPS and UPS retail divisor, and never mentioned the USPS one-cubic-foot threshold; the large-package flag's 'usually well above' text was false for heavy cartons; the explainer and page define girth as L + 2(W+H).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a seller choosing a carton for a UPS/FedEx ground SKU: enter box and weight, read billable weight, air pounds and target cube: works and the lever is genuinely useful. Gaps a shipper hits in the first hour: a USPS Ground Advantage / Priority shipper entering 166 for a small box is told it bills on dimensional weight when USPS bills actual; long thin items (rods, rugs, ski boxes) over 96 in were not flagged as Large Package; Additional Handling by actual weight (>50 lb) is not flagged (disclosed as 'from dimensions alone'); no metric/international divisor (cm, 5000/6000).
evidence.domain: Matches carrier practice on the core formula: nearest-whole-inch rounding before cubing, ceiling to the next pound per package, max(actual, dim), AH thresholds 48/30/105 strict 'exceeds', maximum 108/165. Departs: Large Package missing the >96 in length trigger (UPS Rate and Service Guide 'Large Package Surcharge'; FedEx 'Oversize'), USPS DIM applies only above 1,728 in3 (USPS DMM / Notice 123, Priority Mail and Ground Advantage), weight-based Additional Handling (>50 lb) absent, and 'girth' used for length plus girth.

defects.what: Large Package band omitted the carriers' 'longest side over 96 in' trigger: a 97x8x8 carton (length+girth 129) was reported as additional handling, understating a large-package surcharge and its 90 lb minimum billable weight for long thin items.

Large-package flag said the minimum billable weight is 'usually well above' the computed billable weight, which is false for heavy or bulky cartons (195 lb at 30x30x30) where the 90 lb minimum does not bind.
Four of five seeded core mutants survived: side rounding up instead of to nearest, '>=' on the large-package threshold, the second-side Additional Handling rule, and fractional air weight.

USPS applies dimensional weight only above 1,728 in3, but the tool applies any divisor to any cube and the copy never says so; README, FAQ and explainer described 166 only as a negotiated divisor when it is the published USPS and UPS retail one. A USPS shipper entering 166 for a 12x12x12 / 2 lb parcel is shown 11 lb.
Additional Handling by actual weight (over 50 lb) is not flagged; disclosed as 'from dimensions alone' but a shipper would expect it.
The value labelled 'girth' (L + 2(W+H)) is what carriers call length plus girth; the page and explainer define girth that way, which contradicts carrier terminology.

heightAtDimWeight's null branch cannot fire for positive inputs although its comment says it returns null when the footprint alone prices above the goods; levers.mjs's 1.5 in threshold does that work instead.

verdict: The core billable-weight arithmetic is right: cube from nearest-inch sides, divided by the divisor, ceiling of the greater, multiplied per package, matched an independent recomputation from the published UPS/FedEx rules on 9 cartons at 139 and 166. It misses the bar on correctness, claims and verification. The worst defect was the surcharge banding: a carton over 96 in long with length plus girth under 130 was reported as additional handling instead of Large Package. The large-package text also overclaimed, 166 was presented as a negotiated divisor only with the USPS 1 cu ft rule never mentioned, and 4 of 5 seeded core mutants survived. Fixed in this session (defects 0-3): the 96 in length trigger and honest flag text in calc.mjs, the USPS/166 wording on the README, page and explainer, and 7 new tests that kill all four surviving mutants (59/59 pass). Still open: weight-based Additional Handling, USPS cube threshold not modelled in the engine, girth terminology.
